title: Olivia Rodrigo Creates Adorable Festival Accessory Line for Daisy Chain Fields With 10 Female Etsy Sellers
summary: The collection features jewelry, playing cards and more.
contentText:
Olivia Rodrigo is getting crafty ahead of her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival in Irvine, Calif., partnering with Etsy to debut a line of accessories, trinkets and more.

Related

Olivia Rodrigo Shares Inspiration Behind Daisy Chain Festival, Teases Possible ‘Landslide’ Duet With Stevie Nicks

As announced Thursday (July 23), the pop star’s collection was brought to life by a group of 10 women who run businesses on the online marketplace. Fans can shop adorable beaded jewelry, bookmarks, pendants, flower crowns, hair clips and patches, as well as souvenirs such as a junk journal kit, playing cards, linocut cards and bookmarks.

“I recently made a video for my song ‘The Cure’ using all handmade props and sets, which really inspired me,” Rodrigo said in a statement. “This collection that I got to create with an incredible group of women brings to life pieces that fit perfectly into the world of Daisy Chain Fields. I love that those attending the festival can work with these artists directly to take home their own individual creation.”

Rodrigo also shot an idyllic video modeling the new collection, the feminine, handmade aesthetic of which matches that of Daisy Chain Fields. Featuring an all-women lineup that includes Stevie Nicks, Chappell Roan, KATSEYE and Doechii, the Aug. 29 event’s proceeds will go in full toward charities that champion women and girls, including Planned Parenthood and the Center for Reproductive Rights.

Fans can shop the Etsy collection both online and in person on the festival grounds later this summer.

“I’ve had a dream of doing this festival for years and i am so ecstatic its finally coming true!!” the Grammy winner said in a statement when she first announced the festival in June. “By bringing together women in music and organizations helping shape a better future for women and girls, I hope we can build a community that inspires hope and positive change.”

The High School Musical: The Musical: The Series alum has been hitting the ground running promoting Daisy Chain Fields, all on the heels of releasing her third album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love , and spending two weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 . The four-time Billboard Hot 100-topping artist also recently sat down with leaders at the Center for Reproductive Rights to discuss some of the most pressing issues it is facing.

She also shared more about her inspirations for creating the festival in a Good Morning America interview. “When I pictured this festival, I had an image in my head of girls sitting underneath a tree, like, making little daisy chains or flower crowns or friendship bracelets,” she told Diane Sawyer. “The first person that I called when I decided that I wanted to do this festival was [Lilith Fair founder] Sarah McLachlan. She’s a total trailblazer and an incredible artist and friend.”
